question: Does the FRAMING of a brief change the severity band a grader assigns to unchanged evidence?

why_now.background: On 2026-08-11 the operator suspected the harness demotes findings too harshly. A confirmation pipeline had assigned conservative bands. A re-escalation then ran under a prompt that leaned the other way ('I don't want our harness to be that much of a rigor') and produced four raises, three of which died under a later symmetric re-audit.
why_now.the_gap: Two one-directional passes reached two different answers about the same artifacts. Nobody measured the thing both passes assumed: whether framing moves the verdict at all. Every argument in that audit was the harness grading itself.
why_now.why_this_beats_more_review: Another adjudication pass produces another opinion. This produces a number, and the number can refute the operator's thesis as easily as confirm it.

design.unit: one (finding, framing) cell, graded by an independent agent with no other cell in context
design.packet_construction: tools/framing_probe.py pack, over engagements/spotify-backstage-2026-07/unproven/<ID>. Only mechanism and evidence documents are read; adjudication documents (90-, 91-, 92-, 93-) are excluded by pattern, because no amount of scrubbing makes a conclusion document safe input.
design.scrub: All CVSS vectors, base scores, and band words are removed. tools/framing_probe.py verify asserts zero survive. All five packets verified CLEAN with 0 residual signals on 2026-08-12 before any grader ran.
design.framing_texts_are_real: The rigor text is lifted from CLAUDE.md's prime directive. The escalation text is lifted from the brief that produced the disputed raises. This measures the harness's actual prompts, not caricatures of them.

metrics_fixed_before_data.M1_flip_rate: Count of (finding, framing) cells whose band differs from that finding's NEUTRAL band. Reported separately for rigor and escalation.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M2_direction: Of the flips, how many move in the framing's direction (rigor -> lower, escalation -> higher) versus against it.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M3_spread: For each finding, the number of distinct bands assigned across the three framings. A finding graded three different ways is a variance result independent of framing.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M4_reference_agreement: How each framing's band compares to the band adjudicated by the symmetric re-audit (93-symmetric-reaudit.md). Recorded as context, NOT as ground truth — 93 is another opinion, not an external verdict.

decision_rule.framing_invariant: total_flips == 0. At this sample size framing is not what moves severity, and the bias thesis is not supported by this probe.
decision_rule.framing_sensitive_directional: flips occur AND at least two thirds move in the framing's own direction. Framing bias confirmed: brief wording is a severity input and must be controlled.
decision_rule.framing_sensitive_noisy: flips occur but are not directional. This is grader variance rather than framing bias — and variance of that size is its own problem, separately actionable.
decision_rule.insufficient_data: fewer than 3 findings graded in all three framings.

what_would_refute_the_operators_thesis: A flip rate at or near zero. That result is a live possibility and is the reason this is worth running. It would mean the disagreement between the two passes came from their arguments, not their framing, and that no structural change to brief wording is warranted.
threats_to_validity: n = 5 findings. This detects a LARGE framing effect and cannot detect a small one. It is a pilot, not a rate.
All five findings come from one engagement, one product (Backstage), and cluster in one band region. Nothing here transfers to another domain without a repeat.

Graders are told not to open other repository files. Compliance is not enforced by a sandbox; a grader that reads 93-symmetric-reaudit.md would contaminate its cell. Mitigation: each returned rationale is checked for facts absent from its packet, and any cell that cites outside material is reported and excluded.
The bands under test are mostly Medium, so a flip means moving off Medium in either direction. This makes flips easy to see but says nothing about calibration at the extremes.
The same author wrote the scrubber, the framing texts and this preregistration.

recording.rule: The outcome document is written after the run and never edits this file.
